name: Pine Paper Talisman Primer (Tùng Chỉ Phù Quyết)
concept: The outer gate's method begins with paper. A student peels birch bark, boils it with pine resin and melted frost, and presses it into sheets, drawing Wood qi from the bark and Water qi from the frost as she works. Only then is she taught a stroke. At the sixth layer she can write a plain ward that holds for a night.
lore: The founder Chiêm Thư Sương taught papermaking before writing, so that her students would know what a ward is made of (V007).

name: Frost Pine Ward Canon (Sương Tùng Phù Kinh)
concept: The pavilion's canon is a talisman method. The cultivator writes her own meridians, stroke by stroke, in Wood ink on a body of Water, so that her qi moves along written paths and can be laid down on paper and lit later. In a fight she lays wards in advance: on herself and on lanterns. They go off when a foe crosses them, and each one burns a little of the paper it was written on.
lore: Written down, unlike anything of the pines' own. Tùng Đào allowed it in 1060 because a ward is a tool and not a teaching (V007). The pavilion knows the line between the two is thinner than the pines think.

name: Lantern Ward Art (Hộ Đăng Quyết)
concept: The art of the ward lanterns that hang in the lake villages. A ward written on the inside of a lantern's paper holds for a whole winter, and when it is lit it keeps out cold, beasts and ice. In a fight the holder gains a Lantern charge: while it is held, the holder regenerates and resists cold, and the foe is slowed and marked.
lore: Made after the ice wall of 1033 flattened Nghênh Nguyệt Trấn (V006), before the pavilion existed, by the founder while she was still a ward-writer of the pines' Array Hall. Văn Hàn Đăng hangs four hundred lanterns a winter.
